summary:
On Earth, fire is predictable. In orbit, flames become quiet blue spheres. Others go out but keep burning as cool flames that no eye or smoke detector can see. NASA has studied this for decades, but the results sit in thousands of files that are hard to search and compare. As crews return to the Moon and head to Mars, one missed flame in a sealed cabin can end a mission.

We built IGNIS to make that archive usable. We ingested NASA PSI investigations (SoFIE, BASS-II, FLEX-2, ACME, SAFFIRE, SAME-R) and NTRS papers into one auditable dataset. A C++20 reduced-order physics core, calibrated to those measurements, simulates ignition, flame spread, extinction limits and hidden cool flames.

Every risk score carries a conformal uncertainty interval and an exact Shapley breakdown. Inputs outside the calibrated range are flagged as extrapolation. A voice-enabled SI copilot answers with the three nearest real NASA runs and can drive the simulation.

The dashboard summarizes each investigation, ranks them by transparent safety risk, and interprets the corpus into fire-safety insights. IGNIS lets future crews learn from decades of NASA data before they leave Earth.
details:
What it does. IGNIS turns NASA's microgravity combustion archive into an interactive fire-safety tool. Python pipelines ingest 14 NASA PSI investigations (SoFIE-GEL, BASS-II, FLEX-2, ACME, SAFFIRE, SAME-R and others) plus NTRS papers into one auditable dataset. A C++20 reduced-order physics core, calibrated to those measurements, simulates ignition, flame spread, extinction limits and hidden cool flames. Every risk score comes with a conformal uncertainty interval and an exact Shapley breakdown. Inputs outside the calibrated range are flagged as extrapolation. A text and voice SI copilot answers from the 3 nearest real NASA runs, with a deterministic offline fallback. The dashboard summarizes, ranks and interprets the investigations.

Benefits and impact. Mission planners can find, compare and rank decades of results in one place. Every number traces back to a NASA record and shows how far to trust it. The tool targets crewed vehicles (ISS, Gateway, Moon, Mars), where invisible cool flames and detector-defeating smoke are the real hazards.

Tools. C++20, CMake, pybind11, Python, FastAPI, WebSocket, MAPIE, Cantera, SHAP, React 19, Vite, Tailwind, GSAP, an OpenAI-compatible LLM gateway, and Whisper speech-to-text. Tests use pytest and vitest.

Creativity. The risk model is a small analytical formula evaluated natively next to the physics, so it needs no ML runtime and its explanations are exact. The copilot is grounded in retrieved real runs before the LLM writes anything. Voice commands drive the simulation directly, and the project is framed as an orbital-shipyard game prototype.

Factors considered. Honest uncertainty, data provenance, reproducibility through a seeded solver and parity tests, graceful offline fallback, and a scope limited to cabins and habitats.
dataRefs: NASA SVS: Studies Fire in Microgravity (SoFIE-GEL)
